name: Jehoiachin
overview: Jehoiachin was a male king of Judah and the son of Eliakim, also known as Jehoiakim. His reign is marked by doing evil in the sight of the LORD, reflecting a period of disobedience and judgment. He is a significant figure in the history of Judah during a time of great turmoil and exile.
namesAndTitles: Jehoiachin's name means 'YHWH supports,' revealing a theologically rich meaning tied to God's support, though the name was not given directly by God. He is also known by the names Jeconiah and Coniah, which carry the same meaning, and he held the title 'King of Judah,' emphasizing his royal role.
familyAndRelationships: Jehoiachin was the son of Eliakim (Jehoiakim) and presumably of Nehushta. He is also inferred to be the father of several individuals including Shealtiel, Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. His exile was carried out by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoiachin's significance lies in his role as a king who led Judah into evil, resulting in divine judgment through exile by Nebuchadnezzar. His reign represents a critical moment in the biblical narrative where the consequences of unfaithfulness to God led to the captivity of Judah. His lineage and kingship are pivotal in understanding the prophetic and historical developments during this era.
